# SENTINEL — Final Research Results and Evidence Log

**Purpose:** document the completed, reproducible benchmark outputs bundled with this release. Values below are read from the saved experiment metadata generated by the project; no target values were edited or generated for presentation.

## 1. Scope and evaluation protocol

SENTINEL contains two distinct benchmark datasets and more than one prediction task:

- **NSL-KDD native task:** five labels — Normal, DoS, Probe, R2L and U2R.
- **UNSW-NB15 native task:** ten labels — Normal, Fuzzers, Analysis, Backdoors, DoS, Exploits, Generic, Reconnaissance, Shellcode and Worms.
- **Binary tasks:** a separate Normal-vs-Attack experiment on each dataset. Binary scores must not be presented as the native multi-class results.

The native comparisons use the official paired training and testing files. Each approach within a dataset is evaluated on the same official test records. The Dynamic prediction path uses model predictions to route records; it does not use the true test class to choose a specialist. Feature subsets are stored with the trained artifact and are not selected from the test labels.

The native UNSW LightGBM search uses an 80/20 stratified, exact-feature-row group holdout drawn from the official training split for candidate selection. Exact duplicate feature rows are kept on one side of that validation split. After selection, models are refit using the complete official training split and evaluated on the official testing split. The official test score is not used as the selection objective (`test_used_for_tuning: false` in the saved metadata).

## 2. Main native multi-class results

### NSL-KDD — five-family task

**Bundled active artifact:** Decision Tree experiment, official train/test files (125,973 training records; 22,544 test records).

| Approach | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Weighted-F1 | Average features processed | Test inference time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All features | 72.88% | 51.01% | 69.38% | 122 | 0.01907 s |
| Fixed features | 72.48% | 51.69% | 68.96% | 42 | 0.00848 s |
| **Dynamic** | **76.98%** | **52.98%** | **72.87%** | 54 | 0.01955 s |

In this saved experiment, Dynamic leads accuracy by **4.11 percentage points over All** and **4.50 points over Fixed**. It also leads macro-F1 by 1.97 and 1.28 points respectively. It processes 55.7% fewer features on average than All, but uses 12 more features than Fixed and is slightly slower than All in the measured test inference run. Therefore, the evidence supports an accuracy advantage for this Dynamic configuration, not a claim that it is best on every resource measure.

### UNSW-NB15 — native ten-category task

**Bundled active artifact:** LightGBM adaptive-specialist experiment, official train/test files (175,341 training records; 82,332 test records; 62 encoded input features).

| Approach | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Weighted-F1 | Average features processed | Test inference time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All features | 66.28% | 45.80% | 72.23% | 62 | 0.9528 s |
| Fixed features | 66.07% | 45.12% | 72.09% | 30 | 0.9275 s |
| **Dynamic** | **66.68%** | **46.06%** | **72.26%** | **26.01** | 1.2465 s |

Dynamic leads accuracy by **0.40 percentage points over All** and **0.61 points over Fixed**. It leads macro-F1 by 0.26 and 0.94 points respectively, and averages about 58.0% fewer features than All and 13.3% fewer than Fixed. The measured Dynamic inference time is higher than both baselines because routing and specialist calls add overhead. The accuracy advantage is real but modest; it should not be described as a large gain.

## 3. Separate binary experiments — not the primary native results

| Dataset / task | Approach | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Average features |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NSL-KDD binary | All | 78.11% | 78.04% | 53 |
| NSL-KDD binary | Fixed | 78.47% | 78.42% | 26 |
| NSL-KDD binary | Dynamic (confidence-gated) | 78.11% | 78.04% | 33.32 |
| UNSW-NB15 binary | All | 92.16% | 92.02% | 62 |
| UNSW-NB15 binary | Fixed | 91.84% | 91.68% | 30 |
| UNSW-NB15 binary | Dynamic (router/specialists) | 91.23% | 91.03% | 24 |

These binary results do **not** show Dynamic winning. The UNSW binary All-feature model is above 90% accuracy, but that result must not be used as evidence for the ten-category task or as a Dynamic win. These binary runs are retained as supplementary experiments for transparency.

A separate saved UNSW-NB15 binary LightGBM experiment is also retained at `backend/artifacts/research/unsw_nb15_binary_lightgbm/`. That independent Normal-vs-Attack run measured **90.83% accuracy** and **90.58% macro-F1** on the same official 82,332-row test file. It is a single binary model result, not an All/Fixed/Dynamic comparison and not the native ten-category score. The 92.16% result above comes from a separate binary All-feature comparison experiment; do not merge the two runs into one table.

## 4. Alternative native NSL-KDD LightGBM trial

A separate LightGBM native five-family experiment is also bundled under `backend/artifacts/research/adaptive_feature_selection/nsl_kdd_native/`. On the official test set it scored:

| Approach | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Average features |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All | 78.54% | 64.48% | 53 |
| Fixed | 76.50% | 58.16% | 26 |
| Dynamic | 75.29% | 55.04% | 21.40 |

This alternative model family did **not** preserve the Dynamic advantage. It is included as a research counter-result, not silently replaced with the better-looking Decision Tree comparison. It demonstrates that the Dynamic design is not automatically superior for every estimator or dataset configuration.

## 5. What can and cannot be claimed

Supported by the bundled results:

1. The saved NSL-KDD Decision Tree comparison shows Dynamic ahead in accuracy and macro-F1.
2. The saved native UNSW-NB15 LightGBM comparison shows Dynamic slightly ahead in accuracy and macro-F1 while processing fewer features.
3. Dynamic inference has additional routing/specialist overhead on UNSW-NB15.
4. The binary comparisons and the alternative NSL-KDD LightGBM trial show that Dynamic does not win every experiment.

Not supported:

- A claim that both native multi-class datasets achieve 85–90% accuracy.
- A claim that Dynamic always outperforms All and Fixed for every classifier, dataset, task or split.
- Using binary Normal-vs-Attack accuracy as the multi-class accuracy.
- Presenting training-side validation scores as held-out test scores.
- Claiming production-grade packet capture, real-time blocking or deployment readiness.

The current native multi-class UNSW-NB15 score is 66.68%, and the current saved NSL-KDD score is 76.98%. These are the actual results in the included model artifacts. A target of 85–90% is an objective for further research, not a measured outcome of this release.

## 6. Reproduction and artifact locations

- Active NSL-KDD artifact: `backend/artifacts/nsl_kdd/model.joblib` and `metadata.json`.
- Active UNSW-NB15 artifact: `backend/artifacts/unsw_nb15/model.joblib` and `metadata.json`.
- Additional experiments: `backend/artifacts/research/adaptive_feature_selection/`.
- Feature selection / validation / refit utilities: `scripts/optimize_adaptive_research.py`, `scripts/fit_lgbm_bundle.py`, `scripts/fit_lgbm_single.py`, `scripts/finish_adaptive_research.py` and `scripts/compare_estimators_validation.py`.
- The `*_native` folders contain the native multi-class experiment records; the `*_binary` folders contain separate binary-task records.

The active project model artifacts are the model files that the application loads. The research-folder artifacts preserve the additional experimental candidates and their metrics for inspection. Selecting a new classifier in the UI and training again will create a new experiment and may replace the corresponding active local model.


## 7. Accuracy-focused final pass (supplementary candidates)

See [`ACCURACY_PASS_RESULTS.md`](ACCURACY_PASS_RESULTS.md) for the complete protocol and interpretation. This pass added full-training-set XGBoost all-feature candidates without replacing the active All/Fixed/Dynamic artifacts: UNSW-NB15 native ten-category achieved 76.99% official-test accuracy (macro-F1 50.90%); NSL-KDD native five-family achieved 76.62% (macro-F1 52.90%). These are supplementary all-feature model-family results, not dynamic-feature-selection results. The 91%+ values in the separate UNSW binary task remain binary-only and must not be presented as native multiclass performance.

## Accuracy redesign continuation — 19 November 2026

The subsequent research pass added hybrid filter/wrapper rankings (Gain Ratio, Mutual Information, correlation ratio, Decision Tree and ExtraTrees importance), learned confidence/correctness routers, full-training forest/boosting comparisons, unlabeled domain weighting, and self-training from unlabeled target features. See `ACCURACY_PASS_STATUS_2026-11-19.md` for the complete benchmark table and protocol boundaries.

This continuation does not meet the requested 80–90% native multiclass target. The best currently reproducible strict-inductive Dynamic result is 77.88% on NSL-KDD, below the 78.31% Fixed result. UNSW-NB15 Dynamic is 76.34%, only 0.004 percentage points above Fixed and not a meaningful gain. The 76.62% NSL-KDD and 76.99% UNSW-NB15 XGBoost candidates are non-adaptive all-feature candidates. No 80–90% result is claimed.
